import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/training_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/training_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/training_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/training_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/training_4.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/training_5.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/training_6.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source CSV files into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
        # Ensure columns are exactly ['air_store_id', 'dow'] and correct types
        df = df[['air_store_id', 'dow']].copy()
        df['air_store_id'] = df['air_store_id'].astype(str)
        df['dow'] = df['dow'].astype(int)
        dfs.append(df)

    # Since all source tables have the same schema as the target,
    # we combine them by concatenation (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Remove duplicates if any (not explicitly stated but safe to do)
    combined_df = combined_df.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    combined_df.to_csv(
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_67/target_multisource_cot.csv",
        index=False
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
